title: The Living Daylights
build: Domark UK release (PAL), disk DAYLIGHTS 200787, G64

exclude: the two screens the game draws on in turn, $4000 and $4400, with their sprite pointers: rebuilt every frame of scrolling. Before init_machine runs, $4000-$41FF holds the start of packed screen 3, which it copies to $0200

the level buffer, rebuilt at every level by unpack_screen from a packed screen: the level's own characters (from $7A00 or later, by screen_dest), the map's 23 rows of 160 columns at $8000 and their colours at $8E60. Before init_machine runs, $8D00-$9CFF holds the packed data it copies to $D000
a stale copy of $DFC0-$DFFF: init_machine copies $8D00-$9CFF to $D000, and unpack_screen's output stops at $9CBF, so nothing reads these bytes
include: RAM under the I/O chips: init_machine copies packed screens there and unpack_screen reads them with $01 = $34
extra: packed screens 3 (The Mansion, from $0200) and 4 (The Fairground, from $0C19), read by huff_decode through a pointer
packed screens 0-2 and 5-9, read by huff_decode through a pointer
the Huffman tree huff_decode walks: flags at $9D00, left children at $9E00, right children at $9F00
sprite shapes, pointers $20-$BF, chosen through pointer tables so nothing references most of them by address
